fact: The brightest jewel of the Southern Cross — and the southernmost first-magnitude star.
bio: Acrux (Alpha Crucis) is a hot blue multiple system about 320 light-years away, the luminous foot of the Southern Cross. Its component stars are young and massive, blazing in blue-white light.
cultural: As the leading star of Crux, Acrux shares in the Southern Cross that appears on the national flags of Australia, New Zealand, Brazil, Papua New Guinea and Samoa. For cultures across the southern hemisphere the Cross is a central navigational and seasonal marker.
